name: Anna Brownell Jameson
bio: Anna Brownell Jameson was born in Dublin in 1794, the eldest daughter of the miniature-painter D. Brownell Murphy. She became a governess at sixteen and in 1825 married Robert Jameson.
She is best known as a writer on art, notably Sacred and Legendary Art. She died at Ealing in 1860.

poems.title: Take me, Mother Earth
poems.author: Anna Brownell Jameson
poems.collection: A Victorian Anthology, 1837–1895, ed. Edmund Clarence Stedman (1895)
poems.text:
Take me, Mother Earth, to thy cold breast,
And fold me there in everlasting rest!
The long day is o'er,
I'm weary, I would sleep;
But deep, deep,
Never to waken more.

I have had joy and sorrow, I have prov'd
What life could give, have lov'd, and been belov'd;
I am sick, and heart-sore,
And weary; let me sleep;
But deep, deep,
Never to waken more.

To thy dark chamber, Mother Earth, I come,
Prepare thy dreamless bed in my last home:
Shut down the marble door,
And leave me! Let me sleep;
But deep, deep,
Never to waken more!
